primitives.name: Feature-Weighted Feature Averaging
primitives.verbatim_quote: FFORMA: XGBoost meta-learner predicts model weights from 43 tsfeatures meta-features, softmax over base learners, weighted-average loss objective with custom gradient G_nm = w_nm(L_nm - L̄_n) and Hessian H_nm ≈ w_nm(L_nm(1-w_nm) - G_nm); hyperparameters via Bayesian optimization (300 runs, GP), early stopping patience 10.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'w_m': 'model weight, dimensionless', 'f_n': 'time-series features vector, dimensionless', 'p_m': 'XGBoost prediction score, dimensionless', 'L_nm': 'loss of model m at time n, dimensionless', 'L̄_n': 'expected loss, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Base learners are independent; meta-features capture predictive signal; XGBoost learns optimal weight function.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When base learner performance diverges significantly, FFORMA may overfit to meta-features.

layer2.mapping: GSE's model probability blending mirrors FFORMA’s feature-weighted averaging using probabilistic forecasts instead of time-series features.
layer2.telemetry: Log-loss improvement over simple averaging on walk-forward validation.

primitives.name: Neural Network Stacking Forecast Blending
primitives.verbatim_quote: - NN-STACK: MLP regression over (base forecasts + Spearman-selected meta-features), ReLU, Adam, MAE loss; deep (11 layers) for Hourly/Weekly, shallow (3×10) elsewhere.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Y_{t-1}': 'base forecasts vector, dimensionless', 'f_{t-1}': 'meta-features vector, dimensionless', 'MLP': 'multilayer perceptron, dimensionless', 'y_t': 'forecasted value, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Base forecasts are informative; stacking learns nonlinear combination; meta-features are selected via Spearman correlation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When base learners are highly heterogeneous, stacking may underperform simple averaging.

layer2.mapping: GSE applies neural stacking to combine model probabilities; uses deep architecture for high-frequency data.
layer2.telemetry: Reduction in MAE over individual base forecasts on out-of-sample data.

primitives.name: Simple Arithmetic Averaging
primitives.verbatim_quote: Methods compared: simple arithmetic averaging (AVG), FFORMA (XGBoost feature-weighted averaging), FFORMS-R (random-forest model selection), FFORMS-G (gradient-boosted model selection), NN-STACK (MLP stacking regression over base forecasts + series statistics), FFORMA-N (MLP softmax model weighting).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'y_{m_t}': 'forecast from model m at time t, dimensionless', 'n': 'number of base models, dimensionless', 'y_t': 'ensemble forecast, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: All models contribute equally; no model-specific uncertainty accounted for.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When models vary widely in accuracy, uniform averaging underperforms weighted strategies.

layer2.mapping: GSE retains simple averaging as fallback when meta-learning fails to improve upon baseline.
layer2.telemetry: Baseline performance for comparison in adaptive fusion logic.

reasoning_traces.think:
FFORMA leverages XGBoost to compute model weights via softmax regression over time-series meta-features, optimizing a custom gradient and Hessian for loss minimization. It assumes that meta-features encode sufficient information to predict model performance. The method is robust to heterogeneity among base learners but risks overfitting if meta-features are noisy or misrepresentative. NN-STACK uses an MLP to regress base forecasts and meta-features into a final prediction, allowing for complex interactions but requiring careful architecture design. Simple averaging serves as a baseline, assuming equal contribution from all models. These primitives form a hierarchy where FFORMA and NN-STACK are adaptive fusion strategies, while AVG provides a stable reference. In GSE, these map to probabilistic model blending where FFORMA-style weights are learned from model probabilities rather than raw features, enabling dynamic state transitions based on confidence and performance variance.
